claims.text: Multi-element segregation concentrated at grain boundaries governs the high-temperature structural stability of high-entropy nanoalloys.
Multi-element grain-boundary segregation governs the high-temperature chemical stability of high-entropy nanoalloys.
Multi-element grain-boundary segregation suppresses grain-boundary migration.
Multi-element grain-boundary segregation suppresses interfacial chemical diffusion.
Engineering alloy composition can promote multi-element grain-boundary decoration through controlled segregation during processing.
At 600–1000 °C, diffusional kinetics relevant to the proposed stabilization mechanism are activated.
Grain boundaries enriched with multiple elements constitute a high-configurational-entropy interfacial phase.
Multi-element-enriched grain boundaries have reduced grain-boundary energy.
Multi-element-enriched grain boundaries have reduced mobility.
Retained multi-element decoration increases local configurational entropy.
Increased local configurational entropy lowers the driving force for grain-boundary migration.
Increased local configurational entropy lowers the driving force for chemical diffusion.
Engineered multi-element grain-boundary segregation will slow grain growth relative to samples without targeted segregation.
Engineered multi-element grain-boundary segregation will produce more stable phase distributions during high-temperature exposure.
Engineered multi-element grain-boundary segregation will improve retention of chemical homogeneity during high-temperature exposure.
High-entropy nanoalloys without targeted grain-boundary segregation will exhibit faster grain growth.
High-entropy nanoalloys without targeted grain-boundary segregation will develop more pronounced chemical inhomogeneity during long-term high-temperature exposure.
Above approximately 1050 °C, extensive atomic interdiffusion or phase transformations are expected to limit the proposed stabilization mechanism.
Extreme mechanical loading may alter the grain-boundary stabilization mechanism.
